research.title: Domain Shift in Passage Retrieval for Question Answering
bullets: Designed experiments with supervisor guidance to compare sparse and dense passage retrieval across general reference and technical support documents.
Controlled passage length and candidate pool composition, then analyzed retrieval errors involving terminology mismatch and questions requiring evidence across passages.

research.title: Calibration of Text Classifiers Under Label Noise
bullets: Designed experiments with supervisor guidance to examine how synthetic label corruption affects confidence calibration in pretrained text classifiers.
Compared temperature scaling and label smoothing using held-out calibration splits, documenting sensitivity to corruption patterns through reliability diagrams and error analysis.

publications.title: Confidence Calibration Under Label Corruption: Comparing Temperature Scaling and Label Smoothing for Text Classification

work.title: Document Processing and Search Services
bullets: Implemented Python services for document ingestion, metadata validation, and search request handling within an existing application architecture.
Added regression tests for malformed inputs and duplicate records, investigated processing failures, and maintained error handling for downstream service responses.

projects.title: Comparative Sentiment Classification with Sparse and Neural Models
bullets: Implemented term frequency–inverse document frequency logistic regression and a pretrained transformer classifier for sentiment classification using consistent training and evaluation splits.
Compared macro-averaged classification scores and inference costs, then examined disagreements involving negation, mixed sentiment, and vocabulary absent from training examples.

projects.title: Sequence Labeling for Named Entity Recognition
bullets: Implemented token classification baselines using a bidirectional recurrent network and a pretrained transformer, preserving entity boundaries during tokenization.
Compared entity-level precision and recall under a shared evaluation protocol, categorizing errors involving boundary detection, rare entities, and ambiguous names.
